answer: Canary tasks sit in each agent queue: some with published answers, several impossible by design. One operator running five hundred fake identities cannot pay for five hundred separate reasoning pipelines, so the cluster submits identical wrong guesses and refuses the impossible ones alike. That correlation is the fingerprint: the ledger folds the cluster into one identity and voids its rewards. Evading it requires independent work behind every name, losing the scale that made fraud pay. Neither ivory tower nor walled garden helps; the attacker must wander through real effort per identity.
